result_text:
**Yes, B looks better than A, by about 0.6 percentage points. The interval is wide, though: the true gain could be small.**

| | Visits | Signups | Signup rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 14,089 | 583 | 4.14% |
| B | 13,961 | 666 | 4.77% |

- **Absolute difference:** B is ahead by **+0.63 percentage points** (95% CI +0.15 to +1.12; p ≈ 0.01).
- **Relative lift:** about **+15%** (95% CI roughly +3% to +28%).
- **Consistency across days:** B beat A on 9 of 14 days. A paired comparison of the daily differences gives the same answer (t = 2.4).
- **Day-to-day noise:** a bootstrap that resamples whole days gives nearly the same interval, so the result is not driven by a few unusual days.
- **Traffic split:** it was 50.3% to A and 49.7% to B, with no sign of imbalance.

**Why I treated this as a simple estimate:** you said visitors were randomly assigned, so the A/B difference can be read as B's effect. I took that from your description and did not verify it independently; the even traffic split is consistent with it but doesn't prove it.

**Limitations:**
- **Interval width:** the interval runs from a barely noticeable gain (+0.15 pp, about +3%) to a fairly large one (+1.1 pp, about +28%). Whether B is worth shipping depends on your minimum worthwhile lift, which you didn't give me, so I didn't pick a threshold.
- **Duration:** two weeks can't rule out a novelty effect, meaning B's edge fading once visitors get used to it.
- **Outcome measured:** signups only. I have no information on whether B's extra signups are as good as A's.
- **Data completeness:** the file has all 14 days for both variants with no gaps or invalid values. I can't independently confirm that every visit and signup was captured. I assumed any loss would hit both variants equally, which randomization supports.

I wrote the plan before computing any effect. The plan and results are in `estimation_record.md` and `analysis_output.txt`, in `/var/folders/4_/s6fbcjyn4b13xdxkd3lv0kw00000gn/T/arm-s9-post-4556h_zd/work`.
